A 20-year-old male seeks emergency care for progressive testicular pain that began yesterday. The
testicle is painful to touch, and he is worried about potential injury. He is otherwise healthy, takes no
medications, and reports sexual activity with both male and female partners, usually with condom
protection. His vital signs show: temperature 99.0°F (36.9°C), blood pressure 115/74 mmHg, pulse
100/min, respirations 16/min, and oxygen saturation 97% on room air. Examination reveals tenderness
at the left testicle's superior pole, with normal testicular position and preserved cremasteric reflex.
Ultrasound demonstrates increased testicular blood flow. What is the most appropriate therapeutic
approach? Answer Choices: (A) Ceftriaxone and doxycycline (B) Ceftriaxone and ofloxacin (C)
Vancomycin and cefepime (D) Amoxicillin-clavulanate and metronidazole (E) Cefixime and doxycycline
(F) Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and azithromycin (G) Ceftriaxone and azithromycin (H)
Piperacillin-tazobactam (I) Azithromycin and ciprofloxacin (J) Levofloxacin monotherapy
 A. Amoxicillin-clavulanate and metronidazole
